records.name: Yoga 4 Philly
records.summary: Philadelphia's chapter of Yoga 4 the World, a nonprofit that teaches yoga and meditation across the city. Its work reaches schools, senior homes and shelters, and it runs donation-based community classes.
records.what_you_do: Take a donation-based community class, ask the chapter to bring yoga to your school or group, or email the chapter to volunteer.

cost.text: Community classes are donation-based. The group's page gives no fixed price.

first_step.how: Open the Y4P Community Classes page on yoga4theworld.org and tap a Philadelphia class flyer. Each flyer links to its registration form.
first_step.basis: Community classes are open to the public and each flyer links to a way to sign up, but class days, times and beginner details appear only on the flyer images, which the page text does not show.
first_step.what_to_expect: The classes are donation-based. The group's pages do not describe a class in words, so email the chapter before your first visit to ask about time, place and level.

records.notes: Class days, times and addresses appear only on the three flyer images on the Y4P Community Classes page, which the page text does not show, so none are recorded. A Free Library of Philadelphia calendar page for Yoga4Philly classes returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A web search surfaced library listings for Yoga4Philly classes, but those pages could not be opened, so no details from them are used. The chapter page's only dated item is its 2019 launch.

records.name: Epic Adventurez
records.summary: A live action roleplay group that plays costumed games with foam gear. Its core event is a Saturday afternoon Capture the Flag game at Clark Park, and it also runs camps and teaches members to craft foam swords and props.
records.what_you_do: Join the Saturday Capture the Flag game at Clark Park, try one of the camps, or learn to craft foam props with the group.

schedule.text: Weekly Capture the Flag game on Saturdays, 1 to 4 pm, at Clark Park. Camps and seasonal events are announced separately.

cost.text: Returning players are invited to donate about $10 on a sliding scale. The site gives no first-visit price.

first_step.how: Sign the participant waiver linked on the Our Programs page, then come to a Saturday Capture the Flag game at Clark Park. Games start at 1 pm.
first_step.basis: The site says it serves people new to live action roleplay, trains new recruits, and asks for a signed waiver before the weekly game.
first_step.what_to_expect: A game runs about three hours on Saturday afternoon. Players form teams and try to take each other's flag using foam play gear, with no referees, so players are trusted to play fair. The group supplies equipment, but the site does not say what a first-timer pays.
first_visit_tips: Sign the waiver before you come, since every player needs one
Bring yourself; the group supplies the foam equipment
Follow the group on Facebook or Discord for game updates

records.notes: The Events page (/participate) returned HTTP 404 and was not used. The calendar lists no dated events. Sojourn (one-day camp), Adventure Camp (week-long) and Gel and Nerf have no dates, prices or ages on the site, so they are not in the schedule. The tier 1 summary described cooperative stories, but the core event is a team game, so the summary was rewritten. Status stays probably_active because no dated items were found.

records.name: Indigenous Education
records.summary: Shares the history of North America's original peoples, with a focus on the Southeast, through videos, online courses and books. It also runs Pathways to Peace and Purpose, a West Philadelphia program with workshops, clean-ups, bike rides and fire circles.
records.what_you_do: Take a self-paced online course, join a Pathways workshop, clean-up or bike ride in West Philadelphia, or donate.

schedule.text: Pathways to Peace and Purpose holds monthly guided bike rides and full moon fire circles in West Philadelphia. Online courses are self-paced with no set times.

cost.text: The course catalog lists two courses at $49.99 each. The site states no fee for Pathways.

first_step.how: Pick a course on the course site linked from indedu.org and enroll there. To ask about Pathways or events, email indeed.edu@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a course on the linked course site, so that way in is clear. The site gives no sign-up steps for Pathways, so the in-person side is less clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The courses are online and self-paced, and the catalog does not say how long each one takes. Pathways is for youth and residents of West Philadelphia and meets for workshops, clean-ups, monthly bike rides and full moon fire circles, but the site gives no schedule or sign-up steps for it.

records.notes: The course catalog lists two courses at $49.99 each and also a music album at $1.99 under the label Course; the album is not counted as a course. The 2026 gala is a PDF with no date in the page text, so it is not in the schedule. The tier 1 record had two copies of the mailing address, one misspelled; one clean copy is kept. Pathways age range, fees and enrollment are not on the site. last_sign_of_life keeps the tier 1 value because the 2026 gala has no month on the page.

records.name: International League of Muslim Women, Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a Muslim women's group. It runs service, charity, and education programs and holds yearly events such as a family luncheon and a convention.
records.what_you_do: Use the Join our community link to reach the contact page, come to a yearly event, or donate.

schedule.text: Yearly gatherings: a membership tea, a grandmother, mother and daughter luncheon, a winter coat drive and a convention. The events page lists dates.

cost.text: The site does not state fees for events or membership.

first_step.how: Subscribe for updates on tilmwpa.org or send a message through the contact page, and ask whether the next membership tea or luncheon is open to newcomers.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to subscribe or contact the group, but it does not say how membership or volunteering works or whether events are open to non-members.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a visit is like. Its events are listed with dates but without times, places or prices, so ask the group before you go.

records.notes: The 31st Annual Convention page and the 2025 luncheon page give no date, time, place or cost. The events page lists nine dated items from September 2025 to May 2026 with no times or places. Two items dated January 1, 2026 look like placeholder dates and were not used. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the site does not say how joining or volunteering works. Partner groups named on the site are in leads_only.

records.name: Mentor Leaders Produce Mentor Leaders
records.summary: A mentoring nonprofit that works with young people ages 10 to 24 through one-on-one and group mentoring, life skills training, and job pathways for top mentees.
records.what_you_do: Young people can join as mentees through a form on the site, or book a call. The site describes mentor roles only in general terms, so volunteer mentoring is not recorded.

cost.text: The site does not state program fees. It lists financial incentives for mentees based on achievement.

first_step.how: Fill in the Join as a Mentee form on mlpml.org, or book the free consultation call from the Book A Call link.
first_step.basis: The first steps are a form and a free call, and the site does not describe what happens after those.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first step is a free consultation call. After that, the site does not say how often mentees meet, how mentors are matched, or what it costs. The site says each mentee is paired with a dedicated male mentor.

records.notes: The programs page names school partnerships for young men, a reentry leadership track for young people returning after system involvement, and coaching services listed by name only. The FAQ is written for single mothers or guardians of boys. The age range of 10 to 24 is from the programs page; residence rules and fees are not stated. The newest dated items are 2025 (annual report and award), with no 2026 news, so status stays probably_active. Phone and email come from the contact page. No volunteer mentor route is on the site.

records.name: Philly CoderDojo
records.summary: Free, volunteer-led coding clubs for young people ages 7 to 17. Sessions meet on Zoom on Saturday mornings, and kids choose what to build while learning from each other and from mentors.
records.what_you_do: Kids register once, then join Saturday Zoom sessions to build projects with volunteer mentors. Adults sign up through the volunteer form and then complete an onboarding step.

schedule.text: Saturday sessions at 11 am on Zoom, about every other Saturday during the school year and monthly in summer. Each session runs about an hour.

cost.text: Free. Donations are optional and accepted through a PayPal link.

requirements.gear: A charged laptop, plus the free software the site lists for setup

first_step.how: Fill in the one-time Dojo Registration form for the young person, linked from phillycoderdojo.com. After that, Zoom links for upcoming sessions arrive by email.
first_step.basis: The site says beginners often start with Scratch or with a simple website, and one registration covers all upcoming sessions.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions run for about an hour on Zoom, from 11 am to noon on Saturdays. Each dojo picks its own topic, kids work through projects with volunteer mentors and each other, and parents may observe or help, especially with younger kids. Sessions are free.
first_visit_tips: Have a charged laptop ready before the session
Create a Unity account and verify its email before anything else
Install Unity Hub and Unity 2022.3.51f1, plus Visual Studio Community 2022 (or Visual Studio Code on a Mac)
Read the Ninja Registration attendee agreement before joining

records.notes: The youth page describes sessions as about every two months during the school year, but the 2026 to 2027 term calendar on the dates page lists Saturdays two weeks apart from September 12, 2026 through June 26, 2027, so the calendar was used. The background check applies to adult mentors on the volunteers page; the page does not say whether parents or attendees need one. The volunteers page mentions in-person dojos, while the dates page says sessions are online. The onboarding page was linked but not read. The site's Eventbrite link is titled 2023 to 2024 and was not used.

records.name: Together We Can Change
records.summary: Makes meals in a home kitchen and brings them by cart to people in need around Philadelphia, and gives out clothing and other essentials.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at upcoming events, donate food, clothes or essentials through the group's wishlists, speak in its Speaker Series, or sponsor. People in need can ask the group for help.

cost.text: Free to volunteer; donations are optional

first_step.how: Call 215-398-2917 or email togetherwecanchange22@gmail.com and say how you would like to help: volunteering at an event, donating food or clothes, speaking in the Speaker Series, or sponsoring.
first_step.basis: The How can I help page lists several ways in, with a phone number and an email address, but it gives no sign-up form and no event-day details.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a volunteer does on event day, where it happens or how long it runs, so ask when you call. The group lists a fundraising gala and ticket sales, but the pages read for this check give no date for either.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you come, since the site has no sign-up form
Ask the time and place of the event you want to join; the site does not list them

records.notes: The upcoming events and calendar pages list no dated events. The gala page shows a 2022 recap and a 2023 gala file with no date text. A ticket link on the upcoming events page points to a 2026 fundraiser, but the page gives no date for it. Status is left at probably_active on the strength of a working site, but the newest dated text is older than a year, so it could be dormant. Event-day volunteer details are not on the site.
